hypothesis: The independent per-option math may amortize OpenMP team overhead on larger inputs. A direct serial branch for budgets of one or less avoids team creation there, while schedule(static) gives larger positive budgets disjoint output indices without changing the Black–Scholes or CND arithmetic. Performance improvement remains unmeasured.

The Black–Scholes iterations are independent, but the baseline does not explicitly communicate lane independence. An OpenMP SIMD loop may vectorize the scalar expressions where the compiler and math support allow it; scalar logf/sqrtf/expf calls remain correct if the compiler instead scalarizes them. Reusing sqrtf(T) and expressing CND's sign choice as a select may also help vectorization. The compiler and runtime will determine whether this improves wall time.

Evaluating the unchanged CND polynomial in Horner form may reduce independent power and coefficient-multiplication work. Explicitly reusing sqrt(T) and v*sqrt(T) may avoid repeated scalar work in d1 and d2. Floating-point rounding may change, and the compiler may already eliminate some repeated work; correctness and any speed effect remain to be measured.

The prior candidate combined CND Horner evaluation with shared sqrt intermediates and was slower than baseline, so its measurements do not isolate Horner's effect. This variant changes only the existing CND polynomial to Horner form while retaining the baseline d1/d2 expressions. Horner may reduce explicit power and multiplication work, though its dependency chain or compiler optimization may erase that benefit. If the arithmetic reduction matters, matched controller timings should improve, most clearly at the larger size; stop this variant if it fails the fixed-tolerance checks or if repeated timings show no improvement at the supplied sizes and thread budgets.

This candidate tests a different dispatch mechanism: use serial execution when count is below 512 times the requested team size, otherwise use a static OpenMP loop, with a direct serial path for budgets of one or less. The hypothesis is that avoiding team setup below this per-thread work threshold helps small calls while preserving parallel execution for the supplied large sizes at budget four. Falsify it with repeated end-to-end measurements for small sizes and the supplied size/budget pairs; discard the cutoff if it does not provide a repeatable gain or regresses the measured configurations.

The prior omp-simd candidate was correct but had a higher measured mean than baseline (0.002766 s vs 0.002488 s), so this tests a contrasting mechanism: explicit four-lane vector arithmetic for Black–Scholes and the CND polynomial while retaining scalar logf/sqrtf/expf calls per lane. If lane arithmetic is a meaningful cost and vector packing is inexpensive, this should reduce wall time against the baseline at both supplied sizes and budgets; if scalar transcendental calls and pack/unpack overhead dominate, it may not. Le calcul par option du noyau c2 est indépendant, et le travail des fonctions mathématiques par groupe de quatre peut être partagé sans changer le SIMD explicite. La prédiction est falsifiée si les quatre configurations ne restent pas correctes ou si les mesures contrôlées ne dépassent pas c2 et les meilleurs candidats de référence.
